transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Redwood CSM) ; Daniel Park (Stratus CTO), Maya Lopez (ML Eng), Evan Chen (Security), Leah Ortiz (Product)

Summary:
- Intro / discovery for Redwood PLG quickstart and question about Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments.
- Stratus wants fast time-to-first-token for product demos, curious about free credits, trial flow, and how to validate latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Security team flagged SOC2, KMS, VPC options, data retention.
- Agreed next steps: send pricing/security docs, create trial with credits, schedule SE deep-dive for benchmarks.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. I'm Alex Morgan from Redwood, our AE for the account, with Priya Shah, our solutions engineer, and Jordan on CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Daniel Park: Good, thanks. Ready to dive in.
[00:09] Maya Lopez: Hi, yeah, excited — we've poked around the quickstart but want to understand performance and operational tradeoffs.
[00:16] Alex Morgan: Great. The goal here is to understand your use cases, timelines, and whether Hosted (our PLG API), Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private (VPC/on-prem) makes sense. Also cover quickstart flow: free credits, time-to-first-token, sample notebooks.
[00:30] Evan Chen: From a security POV we need SOC2 evidence, audit logs, and must know about KMS and whether keys leave our VPC.
[00:38] Priya Shah: Totally, we'll cover all that. Quick note — this call will be a mix of product and technical. We'll aim to leave with concrete next steps.

[02:05] Alex Morgan: Daniel, can you give us the context — what are you building and the primary constraints?
[02:12] Daniel Park: Sure. Stratus builds an ML assistant embedded into our dashboard — lots of internal and external queries. Primary constraints are latency for demo users, predictable cost as we scale, and enterprise security for a subset of customers. We want something we can spin up quickly for product demos (time-to-first-token) and then evaluate longer-term; Dedicated sounds interesting if traffic patterns justify it.
[02:39] Alex Morgan: Makes sense. When you say time-to-first-token, what's your target?
[02:44] Leah Ortiz: Ideally under 300ms for small prompts in demos, but for heavier generation 600–800ms is acceptable.
[02:52] Maya Lopez: For production, we aim for p95 < 400ms for typical assistant queries at 5–10 QPS per model.

[04:10] Priya Shah: Okay. Quickstart: with Redwood Hosted API you can sign up, spin up an API key, and start sending calls in minutes. We offer free trial credits for PLG signups — Jordan will create the trial and apply credits after the call. The API supports streaming responses, function/tool calling, and embeddings. For time-to-first-token, the main levers are model choice, sequence length, and whether you use prefix caching or a dedicated instance.
[04:38] Maya Lopez: Are the free credits usable against Dedicated? Or only Hosted?
[04:44] Jordan Patel: The credits are for Hosted self-serve only; Dedicated is typically contracted — we can do a POC credit discussion but normally Dedicated requires a reserved commitment.
[04:54] Daniel Park: Ok, we probably will start on Hosted to validate product-market fit and then look at Dedicated if latency/cost needs it.

[06:02] Evan Chen: On the security side, question — if we use Hosted, where is data stored and what's retention? We have customers that require 30-day retention maximum and cannot allow logs to be used for model training.
[06:16] Priya Shah: Hosted has configurable retention settings and a no-training option; by default Redwood does not use customer data to train shared models. We offer audit logs and per-tenant logging with RBAC, and we integrate with KMS for key management. For stricter requirements, Private (VPC/on-prem) keeps everything in your network.
[06:36] Evan Chen: Do you support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) so keys never leave our HSM?
[06:40] Priya Shah: Yes, we support KMS integrations and HSM/BYOK for Private and Dedicated customers. For Hosted we have KMS integrations as well; keys are managed per account depending on plan. We'll send the security whitepaper and the SOC2 report after the call.

[08:10] Alex Morgan: On pricing — Hosted is usage-based (per token + embeddings). Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. We can model expected unit economics given your QPS and prompt sizes.
[08:25] Maya Lopez: Could you share sample pricing ranges for Dedicated? We need to do a rough cost comparison vs running our own infra.
[08:31] Alex Morgan: Absolutely, I'll share a pricing sheet with SKUs and cost-per-inference examples. We can also run a quick benchmark to compare latency/cost to a self-hosted baseline.

[10:02] Daniel Park: For benchmarking, we want to test time-to-first-token, steady-state throughput with batching, and KV cache effectiveness.
[10:10] Priya Shah: Perfect. For that, we'll propose a short SE-led benchmark: 1) run a multi-model workload (short prompts, long prompts), 2) measure cold vs warm start, 3) test prefix caching and batching configurations. We'll provide a test script.
[10:28] Maya Lopez: For batching — how deterministic is latency with batching? We worry about increased tail latency if batching is aggressive.
[10:35] Priya Shah: Redwood's serving runtime supports adaptive batching based on latency SLOs and traffic patterns; you can set a max batch latency and target p95. There are knobs to tune for throughput vs latency. Also caching significantly reduces per-token cost and latency for repeated prefixes.

[12:00] Leah Ortiz: What's the rollout path — say we start on Hosted with PLG, then move to Dedicated. How hard is that migration?
[12:08] Priya Shah: It's designed to be smooth — same API and models across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. You can pin model versions and change routing policies. The biggest work is capacity planning and data egress/security setup for Dedicated/Private. We can provide a migration playbook.

[14:05] Evan Chen: About compliance — do you have SOC2 and ISO reports? And do you support SAML SSO and SCIM?
[14:14] Jordan Patel: Yes, SOC2 Type II, ISO attestation available; we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. We'll share links to the compliance docs and our security whitepaper.

[15:40] Daniel Park: One more technical question — model variants and quantization. We sometimes want lower-cost quantized models if quality is ok. How easy is it to switch?
[15:50] Priya Shah: We maintain a model catalog with compatible variants; runtime selects kernels and quantization profiles. Switching generally is an API config change and a rollout can be canaryed. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per workload.

[18:20] Maya Lopez: Any gotchas for multi-tenant usage? We will have enterprise customers with different data residency and security needs.
[18:30] Priya Shah: For multi-tenant, you can have per-customer routing policies, separate tenants in Dedicated, and VPCs or on-prem for the highest isolation. We also offer per-tenant cost/latency dashboards in the Console.

[20:10] Alex Morgan: Quick demo notes — we'll email a quickstart notebook and a cURL example to get you to first token in under 5 minutes. Jordan will create the account and seed free credits.
[20:25] Jordan Patel: I'll send the onboarding link and invite now, expect the email in the next hour.

[22:05] Evan Chen: Regarding logs and audit — can we forward logs into our SIEM and have raw request traces?
[22:12] Priya Shah: Yes, we provide trace hooks, exportable logs, and integrations with common SIEMs. For Private, we can ship logs directly into your logging pipeline.

[25:00] Daniel Park: Let's talk timeline — we're trying to validate in the next 2–3 weeks to decide on a Q3 rollout. Is that realistic?
[25:10] Alex Morgan: Yes, start on Hosted with quickstart and bench in week 1, then evaluate Dedicated POC in week 2 if needed. We'll aim for the SE deep-dive next week.

[27:30] Maya Lopez: A note on model size — what are the memory/latency tradeoffs for 7B vs 70B models on Redwood?
[27:40] Priya Shah: Short answer: smaller models give much faster token latency and lower cost. Our catalog includes performance profiles — e.g., a 7B optimized quantized variant often hits significantly lower p95 latency. We'll attach a performance profile doc.

[30:00] Alex Morgan: Anything else we should know about your procurement or legal timeframe?
[30:05] Daniel Park: Contracting will be fairly standard; our procurement can move once the security checklist is satisfied. We may need a DPA addendum for data residency.

[32:40] Leah Ortiz: For the demo experience: is there an embeddable widget or do we need to build a client?
[32:47] Priya Shah: We have reference clients and SDKs for popular frameworks, plus a simple embeddable example. We'll share the reference app repo link.

[35:00] Jordan Patel: I'll note action items: apply credits, send onboarding, share SOC2, pricing. Priya will prepare bench plan. Alex will follow up on pricing and Dedicated options.

[36:30] Evan Chen: One more quick question — do you have a policy for data deletion on request? Some of our customers require deletion within X days.
[36:40] Priya Shah: Yes, we support data deletion API and configurable retention windows per tenant. We'll include the retention and deletion SLAs in the security packet.

[39:00] Maya Lopez: Great. For the SE deep-dive — I'd like to run a script that simulates repeated assistant prompts and measure KV cache hit rates — is that doable?
[39:10] Priya Shah: Definitely. We'll provide a script and can run it with you. We'll instrument cache hit metrics so you can see the improvement.

[41:20] Daniel Park: Thanks, this was helpful. We'll expect the trial and docs and try to run initial tests this week.
[41:28] Alex Morgan: Perfect — we'll send the pack and schedule the SE session. Thanks everyone for your time.
[41:34] Leah Ortiz: Thanks all.
[41:36] Jordan Patel: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
